segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Hello. This is Real Easy English, the podcast where we have conversations in easy English to help you learn. I'm Beth.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Neil. Remember, you can find all the vocabulary for this episode and a text version on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: How are you today, Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very well, thank you, Beth. How are you?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm good, thank you. What is the topic of our conversation today?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, today, Beth, we're talking about schools. We'll talk about our favourite subjects and what qualifications we have.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK, Neil. First, can you explain the word qualifications?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes. A qualification is an official record that you have successfully done an exam or training for something.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, for example, you can receive a qualification in speaking English if you pass a certain exam.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK, great. So, Neil, what qualifications did you do at school?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well I took all of the normal exams we do in the UK GCSEs and then A these are school exams And then university degrees How about you

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah I am the same I went to school in the UK and did all of the same exams

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: probably that you did. Did you like school?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, I did like school. I think I just like being with

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: my friends and I thought most subjects were quite interesting.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, I think I'm the same.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What were your favourite subjects, Beth?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I really liked English, which sounds

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: quite predictable because now English is part of my job. But I also quite liked textiles,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: which was a subject all about how to make clothes and I made a hat.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So it was quite a practical subject and I enjoyed that.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Do you still wear the hat?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I do not. It was not a good hat.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What was your favourite subject?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I also liked English but I think my favourite subject was history.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK. What about your least favourite subject?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's easy. Maths. I hate maths.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: You still hate maths

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I still hate maths So in this conversation about school we used words like quite very and really

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Quite good means a little bit good.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Very good and really good mean a lot.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, for example, Neil, I quite like history, but you really like history.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: You liked it a lot at school, whereas I liked it a bit.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, did you not like maths because you weren't very good at it?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, I think I was really bad at maths and I didn't like it because I found it very hard.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How about you?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I quite liked maths.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I don't think there was a subject that I didn't really like.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, Beth, it sounds like you were good at everything at school and worked hard.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, do you think you were a nerd?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, a nerd is an informal word for somebody who is very good at school.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, was I a nerd?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, I did enjoy school and I worked hard.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: and one time my friend and I asked our teacher why we hadn been given full marks for a presentation And then she said oh I just give you full marks I think that was probably quite a nerdy

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: thing to do. So maybe.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's very nerdy, Beth.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Let's look at the vocabulary we learned during the conversation.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We had qualification, a record that you have completed an exam or a course.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We had quite. This usually means a little.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Very and really are both used to mean a lot.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, for example, I'm very good at maths.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And nerd, which is an informal word for someone who is good at school, like you, Beth.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Thanks.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And thanks for listening to Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We'll be back next week to talk about our weekend plans.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Until then, you can find more programmes to improve your English on our website.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Why not try some of our dramas and stories? Visit

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Bye for now.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Goodbye.
